SLOOS-informed adjustment: The April 2022 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates bank credit channels were still supportive in Q1—banks eased standards for C&I loans (especially to large and middle‑market firms) and for multifamily CRE, with stronger business loan demand tied to inventory, A/R, plant, and equipment financing. On the consumer side, standards eased for credit cards and demand rose for auto loans and HELOCs, though demand for RRE mortgages weakened. Foreign banks reported some C&I tightening. Taken together, SLOOS suggests credit availability and demand were not yet a near-term drag, partially offsetting the FSR’s more cautious risk tone and the Fed’s hawkish stance. This implies a still‑negative overall sentiment given elevated inflation and geopolitical/supply shocks, but somewhat less negative than the FSR‑only assessment.
